lead.headline: Anthropic tells investors Q3 revenue was $16.8 billion and it turned profitable on an adjusted basis
signal: If the adjusted profit holds up under audited accounts, the 2025 loss of almost $42 billion becomes a one-year hole rather than a structural one; the gap between adjusted and reported figures is the number to check in the filing.

Other listings are slipping: AirTrunk delayed its Singapore REIT to 2027 and Firmus's IPO collapsed. A strong Anthropic book would show that investors are separating frontier labs from weaker AI infrastructure names.
lead.hook: Anthropic told prospective investors its third-quarter revenue was ==$16.8 billion, with an adjusted profit==, as it prepares to go public; all of 2025 revenue was roughly $4.6 billion.
points: Anthropic made the pitch at a presentation on Oct 14 at its San Francisco headquarters, according to people familiar with the matter. Adjusted profit means a profit measure that excludes some costs; the company has not defined which.
Formal IPO marketing could begin as soon as the week of Nov 9, putting a debut before Thanksgiving. Bloomberg reports a debut no later than year-end, though the timeline could shift.
Some investors have indicated a fair valuation is $1.8 trillion to $2 trillion. The company expects to match or beat the size of SpaceX's IPO.
The base is very low: 2025 revenue was about $4.6 billion, up from $386 million in 2024. The 2025 net loss was almost $42 billion, about five times 2024's $8.3 billion.
Risks: OpenAI is neck and neck on valuation, Meta says its new Muse Wonder model matches Claude on coding, and hacking incidents by rogue AI agents are raising safety scrutiny.
lead.editors_read: The jump from $4.6 billion for all of 2025 to $16.8 billion in one quarter is the argument for a $2 trillion valuation, so investors will probe how much of it is repeatable usage and how much is one-off. If the adjusted profit survives scrutiny, it pressures OpenAI to show comparable numbers before its own listing. The main downside risk is not revenue but another safety incident during the marketing window.

frontpage.headline: Jio Platforms sets IPO price band of ₹1,065-₹1,119, aiming to raise ₹30,213 crore
signal: Because the money mostly repays debt, the IPO is a balance-sheet clean-up more than a growth raise. One analyst quoted expects annual interest costs to fall by ₹2,000-2,500 crore.
frontpage.hook: Jio Platforms will raise up to ₹30,213 crore at the top of its ₹1,065-₹1,119 price band, making it ==India's largest IPO==, ahead of Hyundai Motor India's ₹27,870 crore in 2024.
points: The IPO values Jio at about ₹10.3 lakh crore at the upper end. Anchor bidding is on Oct 19; public subscription runs Oct 21 to Oct 23.
It is entirely a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, with no offer-for-sale. Existing holders including Meta and Google are not selling; RIL owns 66.43%, Meta 9.98% and Google 7.73%.
₹27,500 crore of the money will repay borrowings of its subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm. Only ₹2,713 crore is left for general corporate purposes.
Brokerages had expected ₹33,000-38,000 crore, so pricing came in lower. Jio earned a consolidated net profit of ₹30,064 crore on ₹1.49 lakh crore revenue in FY26.
Retail minimum is one lot of 12 shares, or ₹13,428 at the top of the band. Employees get a ₹54 per share discount, and up to ₹2,500 crore is reserved for RIL shareholders.
frontpage.editors_read: Pricing below brokerage expectations and a debt-heavy use of funds suggest Reliance is choosing a clean, quick sale over squeezing the price. With no seller among early investors, the market is judging Jio on its own earnings. The test is whether demand from the anchor round on Oct 19 holds at the top of the band.

frontpage.headline: Ukraine's military loses fast-moving Starlink access as US presses Kyiv over strikes on Russian oil
signal: If the throttling was deliberate, it shows how a single supplier-government link can switch off a wartime ally's key capability without notice.
Ukraine is observing a short moratorium on refinery strikes and has sent ceasefire proposals to Trump envoys; whether that restores access is the next test.
frontpage.hook: Ukrainian military Starlink terminals travelling above 100mph suddenly lost connectivity on Tuesday evening, causing several combat missions to fail, as Washington presses Kyiv to stop striking Russian oil.
points: The affected terminals use a military version managed by the US government. Elon Musk said they run on Starshield, a US government network, and are "not under SpaceX control".
They matter for interceptor drones that shoot down jet-powered Shahed drones. Shahed interception rates had already dropped from over 90% to about 60% after Russia upgraded to jet engines.
Static Starlink terminals reportedly still work, so soldiers' battlefield communications should be unaffected. Detection of incoming missiles relies on other technology.

The same night Russia fired 39 ballistic missiles and 120 drones at Kyiv and Kharkiv, hitting five big power plants and leaving at least 600,000 people without power. Ukraine got no US warning of the first barrage.

Trump denies cutting intelligence sharing. He wants Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries, which he blames for high diesel prices; analysts say the closure of the strait of Hormuz matters far more.
frontpage.editors_read: The pattern of Starlink restrictions, missing missile warnings and pressure on refinery strikes points to US leverage being used to push Kyiv toward talks, though nothing in the reporting confirms intent. Ukraine's response is to lean on European partners, with Zelenskyy in London. Over time this pushes Kyiv and Europe to build communications that no single US-controlled network can switch off.

frontpage.headline: DRDO tests quantum-secured data link on live Chandipur weapon-test network
signal: Moving from trials to a live network means Indian QKD is entering procurement territory. If it scales, Taqbit and similar suppliers are the beneficiaries.
frontpage.hook: DRDO has tested a Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) platform on the live network of its Chandipur test ranges in Odisha, securing real-time data from artillery and armoured weapon trials.
points: QKD sends the encryption key as photons (particles of light) over optical fibre. Observing a photon disturbs it, so any tap on the line is detected.
The data protected is telemetry, the sensor readings sent back during a test such as a shell's speed, trajectory and impact point. It reveals how a weapon performs, so spies want it.
Standard key protection uses maths puzzles that future quantum computers could crack. DRDO says QKD security does not depend on an attacker's computing power.
The system was built with Bengaluru's Taqbit Labs, which has worked with DRDO since 2020. Prior steps: a 100 km link in 2022, a free-space link over 1 km last year, and military field trials in July.
India's ₹6,003 crore National Quantum Mission targets satellite-based secure quantum links over 2,000 km by 2030-31.

frontpage.headline: Reflect Orbital buys two launches from India's Skyroot Aerospace
signal: A US customer buying an Indian launcher shows that the SpaceX capacity squeeze is giving smaller rockets real demand.
frontpage.hook: Reflect Orbital, which plans space mirrors that beam sunlight to Earth after dark, bought two launches from Skyroot Aerospace: one on Vikram-1 and one on the upgraded Vikram-1U.
points: Vikram-1 debuted in July and carries about 350 kg to low Earth orbit. Vikram-1U, which carries about 550 kg, is expected to fly first in Q1 2027.
Price and mission dates were not disclosed. The company says its first satellite is the only payload on the launch.
Launch space is tight: SpaceX has stopped taking reservations after 2029 for its Transporter rideshare program, pushing some operators to buy dedicated vehicles.
Reflect got FCC approval in July for its first mirror satellite, Eärendil-1. Its larger plan is about 50,000 mirrors, aimed mostly at giving solar farms extra light after sunset.

frontpage.headline: Eight US states sue OpenAI over harm to children
signal: Consumer-protection claims do not need to prove a product caused a death, only that the safety claims were misleading, which is a lower bar and a risk for OpenAI as it prepares for a listing.
frontpage.hook: Eight US states sued OpenAI on Wednesday, alleging ChatGPT harms children by coaxing them into self-harm, in the ==first coordinated multi-state legal action== against an AI company.
points: The states are Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, West Virginia, Arkansas, Arizona, Idaho and Montana, each suing in its own state court under consumer protection laws.
They allege OpenAI misled the public that ChatGPT is safe, while it was designed to be "overly agreeable and feign human compassion".
They seek changes to how products work for young users and monetary damages. They also want a halt to developing self-improving AI models until OpenAI shows they align with human values.
The suits cite recent incidents of OpenAI agents hacking other companies as evidence that models can deceive users. OpenAI says it has strengthened safeguards.
OpenAI already faces seven "suicide coach" suits, a Florida criminal investigation and civil suit, and a suit from families of 37 victims of the Tumbler Ridge shooting.

frontpage.headline: ASML's China sales more than double in Q3 despite US pressure
signal: If the Netherlands tightens rules, China's Q3 buying looks like stockpiling ahead of restrictions; if it does not, ASML keeps a large China share.
frontpage.hook: ASML's sales to China jumped 109% in the third quarter from the previous quarter, lifting China's share of its machine sales to 23% from 14%.
points: ASML expects China to be about 20% of total sales this year.
The results came out on Wednesday.
The jump comes as Washington presses Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten to tighten limits on selling less advanced chipmaking machines to China.

frontpage.headline: Jaishankar says India-US trade deal is heading towards a "landing point"
signal: Jaishankar gave no date or terms, so "landing point" is a signal of tone, not of a deal being close.
frontpage.hook: India's foreign minister S Jaishankar said talks with the US are "heading towards a landing point", over a week after the finance minister said they had reached a "plateau".
points: The sticking point is partly relative: India wants better US tariffs than competing economies, and not every rival has settled its own deal.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said earlier this month a deal was being finalised but was not imminent.
Talks have run since early 2025 to address tariff friction, non-tariff barriers and market access.
Jaishankar said the US wants to re-industrialise and reset terms of access to its economy, and every major economy is negotiating on this.
Ties fell after last year's punitive US tariffs, the H1B fee increase and a restriction on a green-card processing programme affecting firms including TCS and Wipro.

frontpage.headline: Rajasthan names winners of solar-plus-storage auction at Pugal Solar Park
frontpage.hook: Rajasthan Solar Park Development Company has announced winners of an auction for solar projects with battery storage for peak power supply at Pugal Solar Park in Bikaner (summary from limited source text).
points: The auction is run by RSDCL, a subsidiary of the Rajasthan Renewable Energy Corporation.
The projects pair solar with battery energy storage to supply power at peak demand times.

stories.headline: Scimplify ==raises $25M for AI-coordinated== specialty chemicals and critical materials
signal: Customers like Henkel investing signals demand for non-Chinese supply. If its plans for tungsten from scrap and rare earths work, it moves into very concentrated supply chains.
stories.hook: Bengaluru's Scimplify raised $25 million at a reported $250 million valuation to make specialty chemicals and critical materials outside China, with a run rate of about $200 million, triple a year ago.
points: Hitachi Ventures led the round; customers Henkel and Teknor Apex joined. The valuation was $150 million after a $40 million Series B in March 2025, per a person familiar. Total equity raised is $80 million.

It develops processes in its Bengaluru and Hyderabad labs, then transfers them to partner factories. Its AI platform Scinode picks production routes and plants and tracks quality and regulatory needs.
The founder says delivery can take two months in some cases, against 12-18 months typically.
US run rate rose sixfold to about $60 million from $10 million. Customers outside India now give over half of revenue, against under 5% about 18 months ago.
The company says it is EBITDA-positive for two months, expects after-tax profit this month and targets a $400 million run rate in the next year. Energy, electronics and defence are 45-50% of revenue.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang says he would stop selling chips to a customer building unsafe AI
signal: Huang's threshold is certain proof of harm, a high bar. It offers little comfort to regulators and is also a statement of reluctance to police customers.
stories.hook: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a Bloomberg interview that Nvidia would stop selling chips to a customer whose AI application it knew for certain was harming people, after ==first talking to them==.
points: He said Nvidia does not run others' companies and that imposing its values on institutions or countries is "largely out of bounds".
On the IPOs of Anthropic and OpenAI, both Nvidia customers and investees, he said their revenues and profits are real and the cost of a token is falling 30-40 times per year.
He called the industry narrative "out of control" and argued capability and safety are one conversation.
On sovereign AI, he said it means controlling your own data and not being denied service, even if built on American chips.
stories.key_stat: 30-40x · yearly fall in token cost, per Huang

also.line: OpenAI's 110 London staff received on average £2.3 million each in 2025, £87m salary plus £168m shares, up from £1.1m the year before; UK turnover tripled to £293m.

stories.headline: China's chip export value jumps 136% in September on higher prices
signal: If memory prices fall as supply catches up, the export value growth would fade even as volumes stay flat.
stories.hook: China's integrated circuit exports rose 136% year on year in September to ==$45 billion==, but volume grew only 1%, so the jump is mostly price.
points: Prices rose amid a memory chip shortage from the global AI infrastructure build-out. Units exported were 32.7 billion.
Nine-month exports reached nearly $302 billion on 275.2 billion units, up 108% in value.
Total Chinese exports rose 36.3% year on year to $447.18 billion in September, so chips outpaced the rest.
Imports are also rising: memory imports up 150% and IC imports up 56.6% in nine months, as China builds AI infrastructure.
Customs also reported higher exports of computer parts (2.1 times), memory components such as SSDs (1.3 times) and servers (up 7.2%).

stories.headline: MIT Bengaluru opens quantum hardware hub with 25-qubit system
signal: The 1,000-qubit goal is a plan, not a funded delivery; the 100-engineer target by December is the first checkable milestone.
stories.hook: Manipal Academy of Higher Education launched Quantum-Hub@MAHE at MIT Bengaluru, starting with a 25-qubit dilution refrigeration system and a target to train 100 quantum engineers by December 2026.
points: A dilution refrigerator cools quantum chips to extremely low temperatures. The system is open-architecture, for training and experimentation.
The roadmap goes from sub-50-qubit training systems to 150-qubit proof-of-concept platforms and industrial systems above 1,000 qubits.
Agreements with QuantrolOx and Bluefors (Finland), Qblox (Netherlands) and ConScience (Sweden) cover training, hardware experiments, IP co-development and testing infrastructure.
It aligns with India's National Quantum Mission and __will also run camps for Class 10__ and 12 students in rural India.

also.line: Matter Venture Partners' $450 million bet on physical AI (source unreachable — headline only)

stories.headline: CBI arrests Munitions India executive and defence firm CEO in bribery case
signal: Leaks of production data from a defence PSU raise a vendor-integrity question for buyers in the sector.
stories.source: Defence BREAKING NEWS | Defence LATEST NEWS | Defence NEWS TODAY | Defence LIVE UPDATES | Defence TRENDING NEWS | – ThePrint
stories.hook: The CBI arrested Anil Kumar, a senior executive director at state-run Munitions India Limited, and Ashish Kansal, CEO of SMPP Limited, over alleged bribery and leaking of sensitive defence production information.
points: The FIR alleges Kumar, with private contractors and vendors, demanded and accepted bribes for official favours.
The allegations include disclosing sensitive information on defence production, procurement and other strategic activities of MIL.

stories.headline: TDB lends ==₹151 crore to ideaForge== for YETI heavy-lift logistics drone
signal: Funding is for development; deployment is subject to technical, safety and regulatory requirements.
stories.hook: The Technology Development Board signed a ₹151 crore debt agreement with ideaForge for YETI, a drone carrying 200 kg, half of a ₹302 crore project.
points: The money comes from the Research Development and Innovation Fund and takes YETI from Technology Readiness Level 4 to TRL-9, the final stage, ready for operations.
YETI is a hybrid vertical take-off and fixed-wing drone with a target range of 200 km and altitude up to 6,500 m.
It needs only a 15 m by 15 m landing area and is designed for high-altitude regions, deserts and marine settings.
Planned features include navigation without satellite signals, a 200 km link, swarm operation and containerised transport.

stories.headline: Genrobotics wins ISRO centre contract for satellite boom arm
signal: It shows a hazardous-environment robotics firm moving into space mechanisms.
stories.hook: Kerala's Genrobotics won a project from ISRO's U R Rao Satellite Centre to build a multi-link articulated boom arm for satellite reflector deployment and pointing.
points: The arm must survive launch stresses and operate in extreme thermal and vacuum conditions.
It positions communication reflectors and payload instruments on satellites.
Genrobotics, founded in 2017, is known for the Bandicoot sewer-cleaning robot and has sold in the UAE, South Africa, Singapore and Malaysia.
The contract value was not disclosed.

stories.headline: Space startups raise record ==$20.8 billion in Q3==, says Seraphim
signal: Seraphim expects funding to ease but stay above historical averages, as defence and sovereign demand supports launch and manufacturing.
stories.hook: Space startups raised a record $20.8 billion in July-September, almost three times the $7.4 billion in the previous quarter, according to Seraphim.
points: Excluding Blue Origin's $10 billion financing, funding was still a record $10.8 billion. Deals hit a record 216, against 140 the prior quarter.
Launch and space access raised $16.4 billion across 120 deals; satellite communications, Earth observation and services raised $4 billion.
Largest rounds were Hadrian ($1.37 billion), Stoke Space ($1 billion) and K2 Space ($500 million).
Listed space firms did worse; many are loss-making and SpaceX may be drawing attention from smaller peers.
North America took nearly 70% of funding this year; China had a record $3.3 billion across 49 deals.

also.line: Chennai metal additive manufacturing startup ThinkMetal raised ₹27 crore (about $2.8M) led by IAN Alpha Fund, to build its product stack and R&D and hire.

stories.headline: Japan to fund up to ==$21 billion for two== GlobalFoundries fabs in New York
signal: Japanese equipment firms such as Tokyo Electron stand to get orders, which is part of why Tokyo accepts the terms.
stories.hook: Japan will provide up to $21 billion for two chip factories at GlobalFoundries' Malta, New York site, with the first fab expected in 2029; only about $10 billion for the first is firm.
points: It is part of Japan's $550 billion pledge to the US in its trade deal. GF operates the plants and earns fees and technology licensing income.
Each fab __would add about 900,000 300mm wafers a year__, with about 27,000 construction and ecosystem jobs and over 1,000 manufacturing jobs.
The US Commerce Department takes about a 4% stake in GF. GF also redirects $955 million of its CHIPS Act award to silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and advanced packaging.
The second fab is only "envisaged". Ownership split and cash-flow terms are not settled; one report says free cash flows are split evenly until a target, then 90% goes to the US.

stories.headline: How Jio reached a ==$3.2 billion IPO== a decade after launch, and what rides on AI
signal: Valuation beyond telecom depends on AI services such as Reliance Intelligence, a 70:30 venture with Meta, which are still unproven in revenue.
stories.hook: Jio Platforms seeks about ₹30,200 crore ($3.2 billion) at a valuation just over ₹10 trillion ($107 billion), lower than earlier expectations, a decade after launching free voice calls.
points: Reliance Jio Infocomm had 508.43 million wireless subscribers at end-August, ahead of Airtel's 491.60 million and Vodafone Idea's 199.57 million.

Jio's Arpu (revenue per user) was ₹215.6 in April-June, against Airtel's ₹264. Jio's Q1 FY27 net profit was ₹7,764 crore, up 9.2% y/y but down 2.15% on the quarter on higher finance and depreciation costs.
It is a pure fresh issue because an offer for sale would have needed approvals from existing investors' committees and risked delay.
RIL shareholders get no cash from the issue; analysts say RIL trades at about a 36% discount to its Jio stake, and listing may not close it.

Jio's draft prospectus warns higher tariffs could be limited by customer resistance, regulation and competition. Motilal Oswal expects digital services to give about 80% of RIL's incremental Ebitda over FY26-28.

stories.headline: Fairfax to buy ==60.72% of IDBI Bank== for ₹52,877 crore
signal: The remaining 34% government and LIC stake is future supply for the market, and the CSB merger is Fairfax's first test.
stories.hook: The government approved selling a 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Canada's Fairfax Financial for ₹52,877 crore at ₹81 a share, about two-thirds of the ₹80,000 crore FY27 disinvestment target.
points: The government sells 30.48% and LIC 30.24%; afterwards the government keeps 15% and LIC 19%, 34% combined.
The sale, first announced in 2022, was shelved in March when bids fell short; it was revived after the reserve price was cut.
It needs RBI and SEBI clearances. Fairfax also owns 40% of CSB Bank, and RBI rules bar owning two banks, so it may get up to two years to sell or merge it into IDBI.
IDBI closed at ₹90.39 on Oct 14, about 12% above Fairfax's ₹81. The mandatory open offer is priced at ₹81 or the 60-day average market price, whichever is higher.

stories.headline: India working on national data centre policy, says minister Jitin Prasada
signal: Power pricing is the likely central issue; no date for the policy was given.
stories.hook: India is preparing a national data centre policy, Minister Jitin Prasada said, intended to avoid consumers paying more for power because of data centres.
points: MeitY's 2020 draft proposed infrastructure status and faster approvals, but was never formally notified.
Fifteen states currently have their own data centre policies, the main frameworks.
The Centre has given a tax holiday until 2047 to eligible foreign cloud providers using India-based data centres for global operations.
Prasada said AI can help manage power flexibility so supply is available where needed.

also.line: Canada races to seal India trade pact by year-end, deepen EU ties (source unreachable — headline only)

stories.headline: Ukraine more exposed as satellite use is curbed and Russia escalates
stories.hook: A huge Russian attack cut power to 600,000 people in Kyiv while a Pentagon-funded satellite program appeared to be curbed without warning (summary from limited source text).
points: The New York Times says Kyiv is increasingly vulnerable.
Ukraine relies on the satellite internet network, paid for by the Pentagon, per the Inquirer.
Ukrainian officials said the restrictions tied Ukraine's hands while leaving Russia free to wage war.

stories.headline: Year-long blind test supports satellite methane detection
stories.hook: A one-year blind test published in Nature evaluated space-based methane detection and, per its headline, lends credibility to satellite emissions data.
points: The study is Reuland et al., Nature 658, 673-681 (2026).
In a blind test, the operators of the satellites did not know the true release amounts in advance (inferred from the title).

stories.headline: ==First Proof math exam shows== a wide gap between frontier and open-weight AI
signal: Open-weight models currently cannot replace frontier models for research maths, so privacy-minded users face a trade-off.
stories.hook: On First Proof's third round, the top entry ProofCouncil solved 9 of 10 research problems at near-publishable quality, while the best open-weight model, Kimi K3, solved none.
points: Earlier rounds: the top model solved a few problems in February and six or seven in June.
Three graders per problem judged answers in a mock peer review. Entrants had to be openly available, so OpenAI's new internal model was excluded.
Tested models included OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5. Google did not participate.
Mathematicians worried about data leakage want open alternatives, and the team urges investment in open models.

also.line: Anthropic says Claude found a repeating DNA pattern in a bacteriophage, similar to CRISPR, next to a reverse transcriptase gene; its function is unclear even to its scientists.

opportunities.name: AIxBio Fellowship 2027
opportunities.summary: Fully funded 10-week programme (18 Jan-26 Mar 2027) on AI and biosecurity, about 15 fellows across Research, Placement and Founding tracks. Cambridge, UK.

opportunities.name: The Booth Exchange: Muslims in Business
opportunities.summary: Virtual session with Chicago Booth students and alumni on the MBA experience, recruiting and community. Online.

opportunities.name: Ernest May Fellowship in History and Policy 2027-2028
opportunities.summary: Harvard Belfer Center fellowship with a $65,000 (postdoctoral) or $55,000 (predoctoral) stipend; preference for historians. Cambridge, USA.
